questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which finding represents a first-line barrier component of innate defense?
choices: Intact skin and mucous membranes
A memory B-cell response after a booster
Antigen-specific cytotoxic T-cell expansion
Long-lived plasma-cell antibody production
questions.explanation: Intact skin and mucous membranes provide immediate, nonspecific barriers to entry. Memory B cells, cytotoxic T-cell expansion, and long-lived plasma cells are adaptive immune mechanisms.

questions.question: Which comparison of innate and adaptive immunity is most accurate?
choices: Innate immunity requires prior exposure, while adaptive immunity never forms memory
Innate immunity responds rapidly to broad patterns, while adaptive immunity is antigen-specific and can form memory
Both systems use only antibodies
Adaptive immunity always acts before barriers and inflammation
questions.explanation: Innate defenses recognize recurring danger patterns rapidly. Adaptive lymphocytes require antigen-specific activation during a first encounter and can generate memory for a faster later response.

questions.question: How does a dendritic cell help connect innate and adaptive immunity?
choices: It becomes an erythrocyte that transports antigen
It processes antigen and presents fragments with activation signals to lymphocytes
It produces every class of immunoglobulin
It permanently suppresses all T-cell activity
questions.explanation: Dendritic cells capture and process antigen, then present antigen fragments and costimulatory signals to lymphocytes in lymphoid tissue, helping initiate a specific adaptive response.

questions.question: Which complement effect makes a microorganism easier for a phagocyte to engulf?
choices: Opsonization
Immune tolerance
Clonal deletion
Epithelial metaplasia
questions.explanation: Opsonization coats a target with molecules that improve recognition and engulfment by phagocytes. Complement can also promote inflammation and damage susceptible membranes.

questions.question: Which adaptive immune cell differentiates into a plasma cell that secretes antibodies?
choices: B lymphocyte
Neutrophil
Natural killer cell
Platelet
questions.explanation: After appropriate activation, B lymphocytes can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells and memory B cells. Neutrophils and natural killer cells are innate effectors.

questions.question: Which teaching statement correctly distinguishes active from passive immunity?
choices: Immune globulin creates durable memory but vaccines do not
Vaccination stimulates the recipient's response and memory, while transferred antibody acts immediately but temporarily
Passive immunity requires clonal expansion before it protects
Maternal IgG is an example of active immunity in the infant
questions.explanation: Vaccination produces active immunity through the recipient's own response and can generate memory. Passive antibody, including maternal IgG or immune globulin, is immediate but temporary.

questions.question: Which mechanism best explains immediate wheezing and urticaria after allergen exposure?
choices: IgE-mediated mast-cell activation
Delayed T-cell injury only
Immune-complex deposition over several days
Failure of hemostasis
questions.explanation: Type I hypersensitivity uses IgE-mediated mast-cell activation and can rapidly cause urticaria, bronchospasm, angioedema, hypotension, and anaphylaxis.

questions.question: Minutes after an IV medication begins, a client develops wheezing, facial swelling and hypotension without a rash. What is the priority action?
choices: Wait for hives before intervening
Stop the suspected trigger, activate emergency help and give intramuscular epinephrine per protocol or order
Give an oral antihistamine and reassess after one hour
Slow the infusion and complete the dose
questions.explanation: Airway and circulatory findings after likely allergen exposure indicate anaphylaxis even without a rash. Prompt emergency response and intramuscular epinephrine are priorities; antihistamines do not replace epinephrine.

questions.question: A client receiving chemotherapy has a temperature of 38.2°C (100.8°F) and a severely reduced absolute neutrophil count but no wound redness. Which interpretation is highest priority?
choices: The absence of redness rules out infection
This may be a time-sensitive infection with a muted inflammatory response
The fever confirms an autoimmune flare
A normal total white blood cell count would eliminate concern
questions.explanation: Severe neutropenia can blunt local and laboratory inflammatory signs. A new fever may be the only early cue of serious infection and requires urgent protocol-based evaluation and treatment.

questions.question: Why is a secondary immune response often faster than the primary response to the same antigen?
choices: The skin permanently stores every antigen
Memory B and T cells formed after the first exposure respond rapidly on re-exposure
Complement becomes antigen-specific for life
Neutrophils begin producing immunoglobulins
questions.explanation: Antigen-specific memory B and T cells persist after the initial response. Re-exposure activates these cells more quickly and effectively than the original naïve-cell response.
